title: What a Realistic TOK Essay Timeline Looks Like…
summary: Build a realistic TOK essay timeline for September-November, covering title choice, planning, drafting, feedback, revision, and final checks.
body_markdown:
A realistic TOK essay timeline for the September-November term spreads the work across approximately **nine focused weeks** . September is for choosing and unpacking the prescribed title, October is for planning and drafting, and November is for feedback, revision, and submission checks.


This schedule is particularly suitable for May-session students beginning the essay during the **IB TOK fall term** . Your school's internal deadlines take priority, so add them to the plan before following this sequence.


### Start With the Official TOK Requirements


The TOK essay is an externally assessed response to **one of six prescribed titles** issued for your examination session. According to the IB's[official TOK overview](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/theory-of-knowledge/) , it has a maximum length of **1,600 words** and contributes **two-thirds of the overall TOK assessment** .


The title must be used exactly as issued. The[official instructions accompanying TOK prescribed titles](https://resources.ibo.org/data/d_0_tokxx_prt_2605_1_e.pdf) explain that examiners expect a clear, coherent, and critical exploration of the selected title.


Keep three distinctions in mind:


- The **IB requirement** is to answer the correct session-specific title within the word limit.
- Your **school deadline** is locally determined and may be earlier than the IB submission date.
- Your **teacher's checkpoints** govern planning discussions, feedback, and authentication.


The IB communicates submission arrangements through schools, as its[TOK deadline guidance](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/theory-of-knowledge/upload-deadline/) explains. Do not plan around dates published by another school.


### The September-November TOK Essay Timeline


Period Main task Concrete outcome


September, weeks 1-2 Compare the prescribed titles Shortlist of two titles


September, weeks 3-4 Choose and unpack one title Key terms, interpretations, and possible AOKs


October, week 1 Investigate examples and perspectives Verified evidence bank


October, week 2 Build the argument One-page analytical outline


October, weeks 3-4 Write the first draft Complete draft close to 1,600 words


November, week 1 Obtain permitted feedback Prioritized revision list


November, weeks 2-3 Revise analysis and evaluation Strong second version


November, week 4 Complete final checks Authenticated, submission-ready essay


### September: Choose Carefully


Read all six titles several times. Do not choose solely because one contains a familiar subject or appears easy. A workable title should support specific examples, contrasting perspectives, and the Areas of Knowledge required by its wording.


Score each possible title from 1-5 for:


- understanding of its central knowledge issue
- quality of examples you can explain accurately
- contrast available between the relevant Areas of Knowledge
- ability to develop a qualified answer


By the end of September, produce a one-page exploration containing the exact title, interpretations of key terms, possible claims, objections, and examples. The[RevisionDojo guide to TOK prescribed titles](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-you-need-to-know-about-the-tok-essay-prescribed-titles) can clarify common demands, but confirm the wording using the document supplied by your school.


Set a decision date after discussing your shortlist with your teacher. Searching indefinitely for a perfect title reduces the time available for analysis and revision.


### Early October: Research and Plan


TOK research is not a competition to collect quotations. Choose accurate examples that reveal how knowledge is produced, justified, interpreted, communicated, or challenged.


For each example, record:


1. What happened, and which reliable source confirms it?
2. What claim about knowledge does it support?
3. What limitation or alternative interpretation challenges that claim?
4. How does it answer the prescribed title?


Then create a one-page outline. A practical structure is an introduction, two substantial Area of Knowledge sections, and a conclusion, although some titles require more integrated comparison. Each section should include a claim, specific example, analysis, alternative perspective, evaluation, and mini-judgement connected to the title.


The[RevisionDojo TOK essay structure guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/structuring-for-success-in-ib-tok-essays) offers a useful framework. It is not a compulsory paragraph formula because the IB assesses the essay holistically.


### Late October: Complete the First Draft


Reserve **two or three sessions each week** , ideally 45-60 minutes each. Regular drafting blocks are more manageable than sacrificing an entire weekend after other coursework has accumulated.


Write the body first if the introduction is blocking progress. Once the argument exists, you can introduce the title precisely and make the conclusion reflect your actual judgement.


A sensible sequence is:


- first Area of Knowledge claim and example
- counter-perspective and evaluation
- second Area of Knowledge claim and example
- counter-perspective and comparison
- introduction and conclusion
- citations and missing links to the title


Prioritize a complete draft over a polished opening. Feedback is more useful when the whole line of reasoning is visible.


### November: Revise the Thinking


Your school will organize its own feedback process, including any required planning and progress interactions. Follow your teacher's instructions about when a draft may be reviewed and what feedback is permitted.


Ask focused questions:


- Where does the essay become descriptive rather than analytical?
- Which example has the weakest connection to the title?
- Have alternative perspectives been evaluated or merely mentioned?
- Is the final judgement consistent with the argument?


Convert feedback into no more than five priorities. Revise the argument, comparisons, and evaluation before editing individual sentences. The[RevisionDojo guide to writing a strong TOK essay](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-write-a-good-tok-essay-a-10-step-guide-for-ib-students) explains how claims, examples, perspectives, and implications should work together.


In the final week, check title focus, factual accuracy, citations, word count, formatting, and academic integrity separately. External sources must be acknowledged using a recognized citation convention.


### If You Are Starting in Late September


Use a four-week recovery schedule rather than attempting everything in one weekend:


Week Required outcome


Week 1 Select the title, interpret key terms, and identify two AOK directions


Week 2 Verify examples and complete an argument plan


Week 3 Write the full draft in four focused sessions


Week 4 Obtain permitted feedback, revise, cite, and proofread


Reduce low-value activity rather than removing revision. Stop collecting examples once you can build and challenge your main claims. A few accurately explained examples are more useful than a catalogue of names and events.


### Common Timeline Mistakes


- **Researching without deciding:** Give every session a deliverable, such as one verified example and a sentence explaining its relevance.
- **Drafting before understanding the title:** Reuse the title's conceptual language throughout your outline and revision notes.
- **Treating the first draft as final:** Leave at least **one full week** for structural revision whenever your calendar permits.
- **Using feedback to replace independent thought:** Feedback may identify problems, but you remain responsible for every claim, interpretation, source, and sentence.


### A Sustainable Weekly Routine


Plan approximately **2-3 focused hours per week** , divided into short sessions. Use one session to develop material, one to test the reasoning, and one to revise existing work.


[Jojo AI and RevisionDojo's TOK resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-ib-tok-resources-exhibition-essay) can help pressure-test a claim or organize a revision checklist. The[TOK Essay Grader](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grader/rubric/tok-essay) can provide a diagnostic view of title focus, support, examples, and perspectives, but it should supplement your teacher's authorized guidance.


### Conclusion


A realistic TOK essay timeline uses September for title analysis, October for research and drafting, and November for feedback and genuine revision. The schedule should produce a concrete outcome each week while respecting school deadlines and academic integrity procedures.


RevisionDojo can support this process without taking ownership of the essay. Use its TOK planning resources early, Jojo AI to test your reasoning, and the TOK Essay Grader after creating an authentic outline or draft.
